html:
An Israeli air defence system that shoots down short range rockets and artillery shells. It was first used in combat in April 2011.

Israel built it after thousands of rockets fell on its north from Hezbollah in the 2006 Lebanon war and on its south from Hamas in the Gaza Strip. The state firm Rafael developed it in a few years. A radar tracks each incoming rocket, a computer works out where it will land, and interceptor missiles are fired only at those heading for towns or key sites. The rest are allowed to fall in open ground.

Israel says it stops around nine in ten of the rockets it engages. The United States has paid a large part of its cost. Each interceptor costs far more than the simple rockets it destroys, and it can be swamped by very large salvos.

It changed the wars around Gaza. Israeli towns were far better protected, which some argue also made short wars easier to sustain without a political solution.
sum: An Israeli air defence system that shoots down short range rockets and artillery shells. It was first used in combat in April 2011.
